Biomass, carbon, and green weight

Source: vignettes/biomass-carbon.Rmd
biomass-carbon.Rmd

biomass() estimates dry and green component masses, aboveground carbon, and carbon dioxide equivalent. The National Scale Volume and Biomass system supplies these equations. green_weight() converts an existing cubic volume using species properties.

Biomass components

nsvb_division_xy() assigns ecological divisions from coordinates. The example inventory supplies longitude and latitude.

## Assign ecological divisions to the shipped inventory
trees <- example_trees_pnw %>%
  mutate(division = nsvb_division_xy(x = longitude, y = latitude)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 5)
tree species dbh ht_simulated division
1 Douglas-fir 25.01 141.8 1240
2 Douglas-fir 10.42 71.0 1240
3 Douglas-fir 12.21 75.2 1240
4 Douglas-fir 6.71 47.3 1240
5 western hemlock 36.09 155.3 1240 
## Estimate component masses in pounds
mass <- biomass(dbh = trees$dbh,
                ht = trees$ht_simulated,
                spcd = trees$spcd,
                division = trees$division,
                id = trees$tree,
                status = TRUE)
id dry_agb_no_foliage dry_stem_wood dry_stem_bark dry_branches dry_foliage carbon carbon_status
1 5733.327 4590.757 669.367 473.203 104.084 2958.397 0
2 613.776 444.109 72.438 97.229 35.257 316.708 0
3 856.009 620.786 101.647 133.575 46.974 441.701 0
4 187.617 121.852 21.844 43.921 19.545 96.810 0
5 12913.767 10193.331 1339.594 1380.842 349.415 6547.280 0

dry_ fields report oven-dry mass. green_ fields include moisture. Imperial calls return pounds, and metric calls return kilograms. The aboveground total excludes foliage, and component fields overlap with totals.

The result includes stump, primary section, secondary section, tip, branch, and foliage components. decay_class and cull apply the biomass system’s tree-condition adjustments. Its product limits are separate from merchandising specifications and selected cuts.

One component and carbon dioxide equivalent

biomass_component() returns one named quantity per tree. co2e() returns metric tons of carbon dioxide equivalent, regardless of the input measurement system.

## Add dry stem mass and carbon dioxide equivalent to tree records
carbon <- trees %>%
  transmute(tree,
            dry_wood_lb = biomass_component(dbh = dbh,
                                            ht = ht_simulated,
                                            spcd = spcd,
                                            division = division,
                                            component = 'dry_stem_wood'),
            carbon_dioxide_t = co2e(dbh = dbh,
                                    ht = ht_simulated,
                                    spcd = spcd,
                                    division = division),
            fraction = carbon_fraction(spcd = spcd))
tree dry_wood_lb carbon_dioxide_t fraction
1 4590.757 4.920 0.516
2 444.109 0.527 0.516
3 620.786 0.735 0.516
4 121.852 0.161 0.516
5 10193.331 10.889 0.507

Carbon excludes foliage. carbon_fraction() returns the live-tree species fraction with a source attribute. Dead-tree carbon follows the decay-specific rules in biomass(). The co2e column in biomass() uses pounds or kilograms, unlike the separate co2e() function.

Weight from cubic volume

green_weight() uses species wood density, bark volume, and moisture properties. Its default returns green wood and attached bark weight from inside-bark cubic volume.

## Convert modeled stem volume to green pounds
weight <- example_trees %>%
  mutate(cubic = stem_volume(dbh = dbh, ht = ht, model = model),
         green_lb = green_weight(volume = cubic, spcd = spcd),
         dry_wood_lb = green_weight(volume = cubic,
                                    spcd = spcd,
                                    component = 'wood',
                                    moisture = 'dry')) %>%
  select(tree, species, cubic, green_lb, dry_wood_lb)
tree species cubic green_lb dry_wood_lb
1 Douglas-fir 16.786 788.882 471.337
2 western hemlock 28.156 1434.825 737.975
3 Douglas-fir 39.208 1842.669 1100.949
4 western hemlock 59.498 3031.964 1559.433
5 Douglas-fir 75.958 3569.866 2132.905
6 western hemlock 136.790 6970.729 3585.262

Property overrides include specific_gravity, moisture_pct, and corresponding bark fields. volume_basis = 'outside' accepts volume including bark. This volume conversion is independent of the fitted biomass system.
